source.title: OneTrans: Unified Feature Interaction and Sequence Modeling with One Transformer in Industrial Recommender
source.authors: Zhao-Qi Zhang; Hao-Lei Pei; Jun Guo; Tian-Yu Wang; Yu-Fei Feng; Hui Sun; Shao-Wei Liu; Aixin Sun

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. It contains conference-template placeholders and inconsistent conference-date text, but is not cut off or otherwise unusable.
record.tranche_reason: It investigates scaling behavior in industrial recommendation models, a different setting from language-model pretraining, and reports performance-versus-compute trends.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the paper's own scaling experiments in Section 4.5 and Figure 3. Comparisons in Tables 2 and 6 measure recommendation performance or online business outcomes, not the scaling-law versions; cited scaling results from other papers are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 reports the authors' own scaling sweeps of industrial recommendation ranking models. They plot CTR ΔUAUC against training FLOPs on a log scale and describe clear log-linear trends. This bears on V5 in a non-text setting. The measure is a ranking metric rather than loss, and the fitted form is linear in log-compute rather than an explicit power law.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that OneTrans shows near log-linear performance gains as width/depth grow, with a steeper performance-compute slope than RankMixer-centric scaling, making it more compute-efficient.
record.recipe_differences: This is an industrial recommendation-ranking scaling study using ΔUAUC and training FLOPs, rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling in parameters, tokens, or compute.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trend differs by model family: OneTrans has a steeper ΔUAUC-versus-FLOPs slope than the RankMixer-centered baseline. The paper also reports that length, depth, and width have different performance-compute trade-offs.

fits_no_version.finding: In OneTrans, increasing token sequence length gives the largest ΔUAUC gains per FLOP. Increasing depth gives larger gains than increasing width (Fig 3a).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In recommender ranking models, the scaling axes (input length, depth, width) give unequal performance-per-compute returns, with depth beating width.

record.peer_reviewed: The Web Conference 2026 (WWW 2026), accepted; camera-ready version forthcoming.
record.problems: The scaling curves are shown in a figure without numerical values, fitted exponents, or uncertainty estimates. The results concern recommendation-ranking metrics, not language-model pretraining loss, and the scaling range is not fully specified in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bear on the listed claim versions. The Figure 3(a) length/depth/width trade-off is described qualitatively, but it does not report a power-law fit; the table and online A/B results measure other outcomes.

untested.parts: Held-out loss, any explicit power-law fit, ranges over several orders of magnitude, image/video modalities, repeated data, and fine-tuning/transfer.
All (no extrapolation from small to large runs).
All for language models. Fig 3(a) compares depth, width and length in a recommender at varying FLOPs, not at fixed parameter count.
All (no comparison of fitting or setup choices).

missing.what: Length, depth and width scaling curves for OneTrans (ΔCTR UAUC vs TFLOPs, e.g. L=6/8/10, D=256/384/512, T=768/1024/2048)
OneTransS (91M, 2.64 TFLOPs) to OneTransL (330M, 8.62 TFLOPs) gains: CTR UAUC +1.77% to +2.79%, described as predictable with capacity

record.verdict_notes: The FLOPs axis in Fig 3(b) appears to be log2-scaled (2^1 to 2^3 TFLOPs), so the tested range is about 4x. There are no fitted exponents or uncertainty for the scaling curves. The record's claim that uncertainty is reported applies only to the A/B tests. The study is not an original source.

No fitting on small runs followed by predictions of much larger runs.

Tests ranking performance in industrial recommendation, not held-out loss; does not test image/video modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream language-model task performance or relationship to pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitting choices or reported fitted exponents, and no test of compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: OneTrans
rows.operation_detail: Jointly widen and deepen OneTrans; plot ΔUAUC against training FLOPs on a log scale.
rows.note: The authors describe a clear log-linear trend. Numerical curve values and fitted exponents are not reported in the text.
rows.check: Figure-only, with no fitted exponent or numbers. The FLOPs axis appears to span only about 2–8 TFLOPs (under one order of magnitude). The measure is ΔUAUC, not held-out loss.

rows.subject: RankMixer+Transformer
rows.size_stated: The RankMixer side is scaled till 1B; parameter count for the plotted points is not otherwise stated.
rows.operation_detail: Scale the RankMixer side of the RankMixer+Transformer baseline; plot ΔUAUC against training FLOPs on a log scale.
rows.note: The authors describe a clear log-linear trend and say its slope is less steep than OneTrans's. Numerical curve values and fitted exponents are not reported in the text.
rows.check: Figure-only. The RankMixer side is scaled 'till 1B' but the per-point sizes are not given. The text calls the slope less steep than OneTrans. Same narrow FLOPs range and non-loss measure as R1.

relationships.condition: Industrial recommendation ranking (OneTrans joint width/depth scaling and the RankMixer+Transformer baseline), CTR ΔUAUC vs training FLOPs, narrow compute range
relationships.reason: Both families show clear log-linear ΔUAUC gains with FLOPs (R1, R2). Evidence is figure-only, spans under one order of magnitude, and uses a ranking metric rather than loss.
relationships.display_finding: Both model families showed clear log-linear ΔUAUC gains with FLOPs over less than one order of magnitude.

relationships.reason: The slope of the scaling trend depends on architecture: RankMixer-side scaling gives a visibly shallower slope than OneTrans (R1 vs R2).
relationships.display_finding: RankMixer-side scaling produced a visibly shallower slope than OneTrans.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: The tested industrial recommendation scaling sweeps
